Title: One of those pesky Reform Body Q's:

Messages.Author: Roger Carhult
Messages.Body:
The card can be played as a reaction card. Does this involve being burned
due to a vote? Say if there's a vote burning a vampire in torpor, can you
play Reform Body then? Is it considered a reaction to an action, or a vote?

Messages.Author: James Coupe
Messages.Body:
In message <9f375i$ift$1...@taliesin.netcom.net.uk>, Roger Carhult
<rogc...@student.luth.se> writes

>The card can be played as a reaction card. Does this involve being burned
>due to a vote? Say if there's a vote burning a vampire in torpor, can you
>play Reform Body then? Is it considered a reaction to an action, or a vote?

I can see no reason why not.

Reaction cards can normally be played during (action based) referenda.
The vampire could play Surprise Influence, because there's an action to
react to - and the action is still there as the effect resolves for
things like Voter Captivation.

As to whether it would be considered either a reaction to an action or a
vote, why is the distinction needed? It could be both.
